newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended strong after trading in a narrow range in the morning, pushed up by futures activity. Gold shares retreated somewhat in the afternoon session after rising in early trade.
"The market was relatively quiet until lunch when futures activity lifted it," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
Dealers said some window-dressing ahead of the unit trust March quarter reporting period could also be responsible for the gains in the market.
Volumes were mediocre and dealers said trade would be quiet ahead of the long weekend. Markets will be closed on Friday for the Human Rights Day public holiday.
They said the market would be quiet until Tuesday when Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan would give an indication of interest rate direction on Tuesday.

Gold shares recovered from Tuesday's bullion price around $346.30 per ounce. The metal recovered to about $349, lifting gold shares. But the market retraced some gains in afternoon trade to end slightly up.
The market was seen taking its cue from Wall Street and the bullion price for direction on Thursday.
The overall index ended up 14.0 points to 7,099.5, the industrial index gained 21.0 points to 8,342.6 points and the gold index added 5.1 points to 1,375.6 points.
There was good demand for Momentum shares which put on 150 cents to 61.50 rand. Absa lost 15 cents to 26.90 rand, Anglo added a rand to 270.50 rand and Lonrho rose 30 cents to 10.50 rand.
On the gold board Freegold lost 50 cents to 34 rand, Dries climbed 25 cents to 43.50 rand, Amgold gained 950 cents to 324 rand and Kloof cut 40 cents to 34 rand.

Near-dated industrial share futures were firmer in late trade as the market overshot on the downside following a weak Wall Street on Wednesday, dealers said. Gold contracts were strong but off the day's highs.
Dealers said the market was building up steadily as every time it fell it did not breach previous lows. It was seen looking to Wall Street for direction for Thursday.
The June all-share contract was at 6,557/70 from 6,540, the industrial contract was at 8,183/87 from 8,161 and the gold contract at 976/80 from 969.
